# Part A - Updated Project Proposal

## A.1 Problem Statement

Organizations increasingly face two converging AI-driven threats that legacy security tools were not designed to address together. First, generative voice-cloning technology has made real-time voice impersonation cheap and accessible, enabling social-engineering attacks (vishing) where an attacker's cloned voice - combined with urgency and authority-pressure language - convinces an employee to disclose credentials or authorize a payment. Second, the same generative-AI wave has introduced a new outbound leakage channel: employees routinely paste proprietary source code, customer PII, and financial data into public AI chat tools, with no inline inspection before that data leaves the organization's network. Existing security products address these problems in isolation - voice-fraud tools do not inspect outgoing AI prompts, and DLP tools do not analyze live call audio - leaving a coverage gap at exactly the point where both risks now originate from the same underlying technology (generative AI).

## A.2 Objectives

- Design and implement a real-time classifier that distinguishes human speech from AI-generated (cloned) speech during live calls, within a latency budget usable in an active conversation.
- Design and implement a multi-label NLP classifier that detects social-engineering conversational patterns (urgency, authority impersonation, credential/payment requests) independent of whether the voice itself is confirmed synthetic.
- Design and implement a data-loss-prevention pipeline that detects and reversibly redacts sensitive data (PII, credentials, source code, financial data) in prompts submitted to public generative-AI tools.
- Fuse both branches into a single, explainable, normalized risk score usable by a non-technical security analyst.
- Deliver a working, demonstrable prototype within the two-semester graduation timeline, evaluated against the accuracy and latency targets defined in this document.

## A.3 Research Gap

Published research and commercial tooling largely treat voice-deepfake detection (ASVspoof-style benchmarks) and text-based DLP/PII redaction as separate research communities with separate evaluation datasets and separate deployment surfaces. There is comparatively little published work - academic or commercial - on a unified risk-scoring layer that normalizes and jointly explains findings from both an audio-authenticity model and a text-based data-leakage model within the same real-time incident. This project's contribution is not a new detection algorithm in either individual branch (both branches deliberately reuse strong, published, pretrained models), but the integration layer, the shared risk taxonomy, and the explainability mechanism that lets a single analyst reason about a cross-channel social-engineering-plus-data-leakage incident as one event.

## A.4 Innovation / Contribution

- Cross-channel correlation: a risk-scoring engine that can, in principle, raise an incident's severity when a voice-authenticity warning and a data-leakage warning occur in temporal proximity - a correlation no single-purpose competitor product currently performs (see A.5).
- Reversible redaction: unlike simple masking, the anonymization layer preserves the ability to restore original values in the AI service's response, keeping the tool usable for legitimate employee workflows rather than only blocking them.
- Bilingual coverage (Arabic + English) for the social-engineering NLP classifier, addressing a gap in most publicly available detection tooling, which is trained overwhelmingly on English corpora.
- Built-in explainability (SHAP) on every Medium/High risk score, so the system produces an auditable justification rather than an opaque number - directly relevant to a compliance/audit use case.

## A.5 Comparison with Existing Solutions

The two closest real, publicly documented reference points are Microsoft Purview (an established enterprise DLP suite that recently added sensitive-data detection inside generative-AI prompts) and DeepTrust (a commercial startup product offering real-time deepfake and social-engineering detection integrated with VoIP platforms such as Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet). Neither offers both capabilities in one product with a unified, explainable score.

| **Capability**                                       | **Microsoft Purview**                  | **DeepTrust**                         | **Our System**                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Real-time voice deepfake detection                   | Not offered                            | Core feature (VoIP integration)       | Yes - RawNet2-based classifier             |
| Social-engineering / vishing language detection      | Not offered                            | Partial (adversarial-AI usage alerts) | Yes - dedicated multi-label NLP classifier |
| DLP / sensitive-data detection in AI prompts         | Core feature (Copilot prompt scanning) | Not offered                           | Yes - regex + NER + code classifier        |
| Reversible redaction with response restoration       | Blocks/labels; no restoration          | Not applicable                        | Yes - AES-256 reversible tokens            |
| Unified cross-channel risk score with explainability | Not offered                            | Not offered                           | Yes - SHAP-based explanation               |

_Note: competitor capabilities above reflect each vendor's own public product documentation as of mid-2026 and should be re-verified close to the defense date, since vendor feature sets change quickly._

## A.6 Why This Project

The project is scoped to be feasible within a two-semester graduation timeline precisely because it deliberately reuses strong pretrained models (Whisper/Faster-Whisper, BERT-family encoders, Presidio/spaCy) rather than training any model from scratch, while still leaving genuine engineering and integration work - real-time audio streaming, cross-branch score fusion, reversible anonymization, and explainability - that is substantial enough to justify a graduation-level defense.

# Part B - AI Subsystem SRS v2.0

This part supersedes Sections 3, 6, and 7 of SRS v1.0. Sections 1, 2, 4, and 5 of SRS v1.0 remain valid and are referenced rather than reproduced in full, except where a specific requirement's wording changes because of an updated model choice (noted in B.6).

## B.1 Model Selection Rationale

Each task below was evaluated against two criteria: (1) achievable accuracy on public benchmarks, and (2) feasibility of fine-tuning/deployment within the compute and time budget of a graduation project. The guiding principle is that the strongest widely-cited model is not automatically the right choice if it meaningfully increases training cost or implementation risk without a proportionate accuracy gain.

| **Task**                       | **Options Considered**                       | **Final Choice**                                                                                                                 | **Rationale**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Voice deepfake detection       | RawNet2 / AASIST / Wav2Vec2-based classifier | Pretrained RawNet2 (fine-tuning optional if higher accuracy is required); AASIST kept as a stretch goal                          | RawNet2 has a lighter compute footprint and mature open-source implementations, with EER competitive enough (low single digits on ASVspoof benchmarks) for a graduation-scope prototype using the pretrained checkpoint alone. AASIST/Wav2Vec2 give marginal accuracy gains but cost more GPU time and engineering effort.     |
| Speech-to-text                 | Whisper / Faster-Whisper                     | Faster-Whisper (CTranslate2 reimplementation)                                                                                    | Same underlying accuracy as Whisper, several times faster inference - directly needed to hit the <3s end-to-end latency target.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Social-engineering NLP         | DistilBERT / mBERT / XLM-R                   | Pretrained mBERT as the primary target (fine-tuning optional if higher accuracy is required); XLM-R as a stretch goal            | mBERT is smaller and faster to adapt on a limited labeled dataset while still supporting Arabic and English adequately, and can be evaluated zero-shot/pretrained before committing to fine-tuning. XLM-R is more accurate cross-lingually but needs a larger fine-tuning corpus than the team is likely to assemble in scope. |
| PII / sensitive-data detection | Presidio + spaCy (unchanged)                 | Presidio + spaCy                                                                                                                 | Stable, well-documented, requires no training from scratch - lowest-risk component of the pipeline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Risk fusion engine             | Rule-based → Isolation Forest → XGBoost      | Rule-based (Phase 1) → XGBoost (Phase 2); Isolation Forest optional as a separate anomaly-flagging layer, not the primary scorer | XGBoost integrates directly with SHAP for the explainability requirement (Section 3.6.3 of v1.0); Isolation Forest is unsupervised and better suited to flagging novel patterns than to supervised risk fusion.                                                                                                                |

Implementation note on RawNet2: the baseline prototype uses the publicly released pretrained RawNet2 checkpoint as-is. Fine-tuning on ASVspoof 2021 / WaveFake is treated as an optional accuracy-improvement step to be attempted only if time permits, not a precondition for a working demo.

Implementation note on mBERT: the baseline prototype uses the pretrained mBERT model directly. Fine-tuning on phishing and synthetic vishing datasets will be performed only if accuracy improvements are required after evaluating the pretrained model's zero-shot performance.

## B.2 Updated Datasets

| **Category**                  | **Datasets**                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Deepfake / voice authenticity | ASVspoof 2019 (LA/DF), ASVspoof 2021, ASVspoof5 (subject to public availability at build time), WaveFake                                                                            |
| Social-engineering NLP        | SMS Spam Collection (UCI), Enron Email Dataset, publicly available phishing-email corpora (e.g., Nazario corpus), plus synthetic scripted call dialogues generated for augmentation |
| PII / NER                     | Presidio default recognizers, ai4privacy/pii-masking-200k (Hugging Face), CoNLL-2003 (NER benchmark)                                                                                |

Important caveat: the email/SMS/phishing corpora above are text-based and were not collected from transcribed phone calls. They are a reasonable starting point for training the urgency / authority-impersonation / credential-request language patterns, but represent a domain gap relative to real spoken conversation - this is tracked explicitly in Section B.8 (Risks) as a mitigation item, not treated as a solved problem.

## B.7 Risks & Limitations

- Domain mismatch: social-engineering training data (email/SMS/phishing corpora) does not originate from transcribed phone calls; language patterns may transfer imperfectly and require fine-tuning on synthetic call dialogues before deployment.
- Adversarial evolution: voice-cloning/vocoder architectures released after the training data was collected may evade the deepfake classifier - a generalization gap well documented in the ASVspoof literature itself.
- Real-world degradation: call-codec compression, background noise, and Arabic dialect variation are all expected to reduce accuracy below clean-benchmark numbers; the telephony-simulated augmentation in v1.0 Section 3.1.4 mitigates but does not eliminate this.
- False positive / false negative trade-off: aggressive redaction thresholds risk blocking legitimate employee work (over-redaction); lenient thresholds risk data leakage - threshold tuning needs a labeled validation set before deployment.
- Cold start for Phase 2: the XGBoost risk-fusion model needs historical labeled incidents that will not exist at project start; the rule-based Phase 1 scorer is therefore the only usable scorer for most of Semester 1.
- Latency risk on CPU-only environments: if GPU access is unavailable during development, end-to-end latency may exceed the <3s target in Section 5.1 - this should be tested early, not assumed.
- Legal/consent constraints on recording and analyzing live call audio may restrict where and how the voice branch can be piloted or where its training/validation data can be collected.

## B.8 Ethical & Legal Considerations

- Privacy by design: consistent with v1.0 Section 5.3, only derived findings (scores, labels, entities) - not raw audio or prompt text - should be retained beyond the short-lived restoration-map lifetime.
- Consent: employees should be informed that call audio and AI-tool prompts are being analyzed, consistent with applicable consent-to-record and workplace-monitoring laws in the deployment jurisdiction.
- Applicable regulation: if piloted in Egypt, the system should be designed with Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 151/2020) in mind; if any data subjects are in the EU, GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) principles on data minimization and purpose limitation apply as well. Both should be confirmed with the academic supervisor or a legal reference rather than assumed.
- Bias and fairness: NLP/NER models trained predominantly on English-language corpora may under-perform on Arabic dialects or non-Western names; periodic fairness auditing is recommended once labeled evaluation data in both languages exists.
- Human-in-the-loop: no automated blocking action should occur without a corresponding audit-log entry (FR-3.6) and an analyst review path for High-risk findings, so the system remains accountable and auditable rather than a black box.

## B.9 Future Work (Trimmed from v1.0 Section 7)

SRS v1.0 Section 7 listed seven optional enhancements. To keep the baseline scope achievable within the graduation timeline, only the following three are retained as active stretch goals; the remaining four are removed from the working scope entirely and listed afterward only for completeness.

### Retained as active stretch goals

- Multilingual social-engineering detection (Arabic + English) - upgrading from mBERT to XLM-R if a sufficiently large bilingual fine-tuning corpus can be assembled (v1.0 Section 7.2).
- Continual learning / feedback loop - allowing analysts to mark alerts as true/false positive from the dashboard to periodically retrain the Phase-2 risk model (v1.0 Section 7.4).
- Confidence calibration - temperature/Platt scaling on the voice-authenticity and NER models so reported confidence values are statistically reliable (v1.0 Section 7.6).

### Removed from scope (kept only as long-term ideas, not planned work)

- Speaker verification / voiceprint enrollment (v1.0 Section 7.1) - adds identity-management and enrollment-UX complexity disproportionate to the graduation timeline.
- Autoencoder-based anomaly detection for novel leakage patterns (v1.0 Section 7.3) - a second unsupervised model to train, validate, and maintain alongside the four already in scope.
- Adaptive per-department risk thresholds (v1.0 Section 7.5) - meaningful only after a real organizational pilot with multiple departments, which is out of reach for a graduation-scope deployment.
- On-device / federated deployment (v1.0 Section 7.7) - federated learning infrastructure is a substantial research project on its own and is not realistic to add on top of the current scope.
